mainTopic: Why leftover יום כיפור animals die (גזירה משום תקלה), and the confession over the שעיר המשתלח and who leads it
overview: The amud opens by finishing the discussion of why a leftover פר and שעיר of יום כיפור are left to die instead of being kept for next year. The 'past its year' reason, with a decree for the פר, is rejected, and רבא explains it as a גזירה משום תקלה. A ברייתא about consecrating things in our time supports him: sacred items with no proper use are destroyed. The גמרא then clarifies that the feared mishap is wrongly offering these animals, since they are still fit to be offered. It proves that fear of תקלה is a dispute between תנאים, using ברייתות about a leftover קרבן פסח and leftover money for it. A new משנה follows: the כהן גדול confesses over the שעיר המשתלח, the crowd bows when it hears the שם המפורש, and the goat is handed to the one who leads it, with a story about ערסלא and the Babylonian Jews. The גמרא discusses why the כהנים are not named in this confession (רבי ירמיה and אביי). It then begins a ברייתא learning from 'איש' that a זר may lead the goat, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A leap month counts as part of the year
steps.stepSummary: The end of a ברייתא about houses in walled cities shows that when a year gets an extra month, the extra month is counted as part of the year.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the year was made a leap year, it is extended for the benefit of the seller.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא about selling a house in a walled city (בתי ערי חומה). It uses this to show that a 'year' always includes an extra leap month.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seller of such a house has one full year to buy it back, and in a leap year he gets the extra month too. So a 'year' means a full year from date to date, even if that is 13 months. Applied here, an animal set aside for this יום כיפור will always be past its year by next יום כיפור, even in a leap year.

keyTerms.meaning: The year was made a leap year (an extra month was added)
The seller
Houses in walled cities, which can only be bought back within one year of the sale

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not about houses for their own sake. The גמרא borrows it only to learn how a 'year' is counted when a leap month is added.

phrases.english: And if [the year] was made a leap year —
phrases.notes: End of a quoted ברייתא about walled-city houses

phrases.english: it is extended for the seller.
phrases.notes: The seller gets the extra month to buy back the house

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם נִתְעַבְּרָה נִתְעַבְּרָה לַמּוֹכֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a proof begun on the previous amud: the leftover animal will be past its year even in a leap year.
steps.raayaObject: That a leftover יום כיפור animal is always past its year by the next יום כיפור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about houses in walled cities: a leap month counts toward the seller's one-year window.

steps.title: The reason works for the goat but not the bull
steps.stepSummary: The 'past its year' reason explains the שעיר, but a פר may be older than a year, so why must it die?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the goat, but for the bull, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reason it just built. It fits the שעיר, but not the פר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שעיר brought as a חטאת must be within its first year, so after a year it is unfit. A פר can be older and still be valid. So the 'past its year' reason cannot explain why a leftover פר has to die.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well for... (opens a partial challenge)
The goat (here, the goat of יום כיפור)
The bull (here, the כהן גדול's bull of יום כיפור)
What is there to say? (asks how the case could be explained)

phrases.english: This works well for the goat,
phrases.notes: The goat must be within its first year

phrases.english: but the bull, what is there to say?
phrases.notes: The bull stays valid even when older than a year

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתִינַח שָׂעִיר פַּר מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the reason from step 1 reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason that the leftover animals die because they pass their year.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason only applies to an animal that becomes unfit after one year. The פר does not, so the reason does not cover it.

steps.title: The bull dies because of a decree tied to the goat
steps.stepSummary: The rabbis decreed the same rule for the פר so that people would not confuse it with the שעיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree: the bull because of the goat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פר really would be fine by Torah law. The rabbis made it die anyway, as a decree tied to the שעיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the two animals are offered together on יום כיפור, the rabbis did not want different rules for them. That way no one would save a leftover שעיר by mistake, thinking it is like the פר.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made to protect against a mistake
Because of / on account of (a protective link to another case)

phrases.english: A decree: the bull on account of the goat.
phrases.notes: The פר gets the שעיר's rule so the two are not confused

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּזֵירָה פַּר אַטּוּ שָׂעִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rabbinic extension: the rule is Torah-based for the שעיר and a decree for the פר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'past its year' reason fails for the פר, so it should not have to die.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פר dies because of a decree, so it is not treated differently from the שעיר.

steps.title: Would we kill an animal just because of a decree?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא protests that a mere rabbinic decree should not be a reason to let a sacred animal die.
steps.simpleTranslation: And because of a decree it should die?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 3. It finds it too harsh to let a קדשים animal die only because of a decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Letting an animal die is an extreme step that destroys sacred property. A decree meant only to prevent confusion seems too weak to demand it. Normally a milder solution, such as letting it graze, would be enough.

keyTerms.meaning: It should die
And because of (here in a surprised, rhetorical tone)

phrases.english: And because of a decree it should die?!
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question that works as a challenge

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִשּׁוּם גְּזֵירָה יָמוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the decree answer given in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the פר dies because of a decree tied to the שעיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A decree against confusion is too weak to justify the harsh result of death. The rabbis would pick a milder way to deal with the animal.

steps.title: An overage sin-offering grazes, it does not die
steps.stepSummary: Even the שעיר should not die, since ריש לקיש rules that a חטאת past its year is sent to graze.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, a sin-offering whose year has passed goes to grazing! As ריש לקיש said: a sin-offering whose year has passed, we view it as if it stands in a cemetery and grazes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second, stronger challenge. Even the שעיר that is past its year should not die; it should be sent to graze.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש teaches that a חטאת past its year is treated as if it stands in a cemetery. A כהן may not go in and bring it out, so it simply grazes there until it gets a blemish. So 'past its year' leads to grazing, not death, and this knocks out the whole reason from steps 1 to 3.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore (adds a second challenge)
A sin-offering whose year has passed
Grazing (left to pasture until it gets a blemish, then redeemed)
A cemetery

steps.confusionAlert: The animal is not really in a cemetery. ריש לקיש means we treat it as if it were somewhere a כהן cannot reach, so it is left alone to graze.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that being past its year does not, by itself, make a חטאת die. A different reason is needed, and רבא provides one next.

phrases.english: And furthermore, a sin-offering whose year has passed —
goes to grazing!
As Reish Lakish said:
phrases.notes: Source for the challenge

phrases.english: A sin-offering whose year has passed,
we view it as though
it stands in a cemetery
phrases.notes: A כהן cannot go in to bring it out

phrases.english: and grazes.
phrases.notes: It grazes until it becomes blemished

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד חַטָּאת שֶׁעִבְּרָה שְׁנָתָהּ לִרְעִיָּה אָזְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge that goes further than step 4 and undercuts the 'past its year' reason itself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The basic reason that the leftover animals die because they passed their year.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The known rule for an overage חטאת, from ריש לקיש, is grazing, not death. So passing its year cannot be why the animal must die.

steps.title: רבא: a decree against misusing sacred property
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a new reason: the animals die because of a decree against a possible mishap.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: it is a decree because of a mishap.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא drops the 'past its year' reason. He says the animals die because of a decree to prevent a mishap (תקלה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a sacred animal is kept alive until next year, something may go wrong with it. Letting it die removes that risk completely. This reason works for the פר and the שעיר alike. Step 11 explains that the specific mishap is offering the animal wrongly, not using it for wool or work.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier approach for a new one)
A mishap, a stumbling block (here, misusing sacred property)
An אמורא who gives the new explanation

steps.whatToRemember: Final reason: the leftover פר and שעיר of יום כיפור are left to die because of גזירה משום תקלה, out of fear that someone will wrongly offer them (see Step 11). It is not because they passed their year.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
It is a decree because of a mishap.
phrases.notes: Fear that people will misuse sacred property

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא גְּזֵירָה מִשּׁוּם תַּקָּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the approach that steps 4 and 5 rejected.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reason: the death is a safeguard against misusing sacred property.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The animals die because they passed their year (plus a decree for the פר).
steps.terutzMaskana: The animals die because of a decree against a possible mishap with them (defined in step 11 as wrongly offering them).

steps.title: No consecrating in our times
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רבא: today one may not consecrate, give a valuation, or dedicate items to the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not consecrate, nor make valuation vows, nor dedicate items in our time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to back up רבא's idea that the rabbis worry about misuse of sacred things. The ברייתא opens with the rule that we do not make things holy today.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With no בית המקדש, sacred items cannot be used for their purpose. They would just sit around, and people might come to misuse them. That is why the ברייתא forbids creating sacred property in the first place.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrate (make something holy for the מקדש)
Make a valuation vow (pledge the Torah-set 'value' of a person to the מקדש)
Dedicate as חרם (devote items to sacred use)
In our time, when there is no בית המקדש

phrases.english: One may not consecrate, nor make valuation vows,
nor dedicate items, in this time.
phrases.notes: Because there is no בית המקדש

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מַקְדִּישִׁין וְאֵין מַעֲרִיכִין וְאֵין מַחְרִימִין בַּזְּמַן הַזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the ברייתא that supports רבא's reason.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's reason of גזירה משום תקלה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about consecrating and dedicating items in our time.

steps.title: How to dispose of items that were consecrated anyway
steps.stepSummary: If someone did consecrate items today, an animal is made to die, perishable items rot, and money's value is thrown into the Dead Sea.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he consecrated, valuated, or dedicated: an animal is uprooted; produce, clothing, and vessels are left to rot; money and metal vessels, he takes their value to the Dead Sea.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with what to do if someone consecrated things anyway. This is the part that proves רבא's point, since a sacred animal is destroyed to prevent misuse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every item is destroyed or made useless so no one can benefit from it. An animal is made to die, perishable things rot, and money or metal is redeemed with its value thrown into ים המלח. This matches רבא exactly: when sacred property has no proper use, the rabbis destroy it rather than risk a תקלה.

keyTerms.meaning: It should be 'uprooted' (made to die)
They should be left to rot
He brings the benefit (its value) away to destroy it
The Dead Sea (anything thrown there is lost for good)

phrases.english: And if he did consecrate, valuate, or dedicate,
an animal — it is uprooted.
phrases.notes: This is the key proof for רבא

phrases.english: produce, clothing, and vessels — they rot,
money and metal vessels —
phrases.notes: These do not rot, so another method is needed

phrases.english: he brings their benefit to the Dead Sea.
phrases.notes: He redeems them and throws the redemption value into the sea

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם הִקְדִּישׁ וְהֶעֱרִיךְ וְהֶחְרִים בְּהֵמָה תֵּיעָקֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 7 and gives the actual proof.
steps.raayaObject: That the rabbis let a sacred animal die to prevent misuse (רבא's תקלה reason).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling 'בהמה תיעקר' for an animal consecrated in our time.

steps.title: What 'uprooting' an animal means
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that 'uprooting' means locking the animal in so that it dies by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is uprooting? He locks the door in front of it, and it dies on its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks what 'uprooting' means and answers right away. You lock the animal in a room and it dies by itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not have the animal actively killed. It simply locks it in, and no reason for this is given here. Instead, it is left without food until it dies. This is the same 'die by itself' death given to the leftover יום כיפור animals.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Uprooting', making the animal die
He locks the door
By itself, on its own

steps.whatToRemember: Sacred property that cannot be used properly is destroyed so no one comes to misuse it. An animal is locked in until it dies on its own.

phrases.english: And what is uprooting?
phrases.notes: Question inside the ברייתא

phrases.english: He locks the door before it,
phrases.notes: The answer follows right away

phrases.english: and it dies on its own.
phrases.notes: From hunger, with no direct killing

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵי זֶה הוּא עִיקּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the word 'תיעקר' from step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the 'uprooting' of a consecrated animal is carried out.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Lock the animal in so it dies on its own.

steps.title: What kind of mishap are we afraid of?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which mishap רבא meant. Neither obvious option seems to work, because each one would apply to all disqualified animals that are sent to graze.
steps.simpleTranslation: A mishap of what? If it is a mishap of offering the animal as a sacrifice, then all animals sent to graze should die too! If it is a mishap of shearing or working the animal, then all animals sent to graze should die too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבא's reason. It asks what 'mishap' means and shows that both possible answers seem to prove too much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many disqualified קדשים are sent to graze until they get a blemish, and they are not left to die. Both kinds of mishap, wrongly offering the animal or using it for wool or work (מעילה), could happen with any of them. So why are only the פר and שעיר left to die?

keyTerms.meaning: A mishap; an accidental sin
Offering an animal on the מזבח
Shearing (the wool), which is forbidden with קדשים
Here: making the animal work, which is forbidden with קדשים
Animals sent out to graze until they get a blemish

phrases.english: A mishap of what?
If it is a mishap of offering it,
then all grazing animals too should be left to die!
If it is a mishap of shearing and working it,
phrases.notes: Using קדשים like this is מעילה.

phrases.english: then all grazing animals too should be left to die!

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּקָּלָה דְּמַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's reason of תקלה from Step 6, now that the ברייתא has supported it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's explanation that the animals die because of a decree against תקלה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every possible mishap would apply equally to all disqualified animals that are sent to graze, so the reason does not explain why only these animals are singled out.

steps.title: The fear is of offering them, because they are still fit to be offered
steps.stepSummary: The fear really is of offering the animal. Other grazing animals cannot be offered, so nobody thinks about bringing them. These animals are still fit for offering, so a person is busy with them and might bring them by mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, the fear is of a mishap of offering. Those other animals, which are not fit for offering, a person is not occupied with them. This one, which is fit for offering, a person is occupied with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It keeps the first option, the fear of offering, and explains why it applies only here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is in the person's mind. An animal that can never be offered does not tempt anyone to bring it. The leftover פר and שעיר are still fit to be offered as a קרבן, so a person stays focused on them, and there is a real risk he will offer them wrongly.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (keeping the first option)
Fit to be offered
Busy with / occupied with (in his thoughts)

phrases.english: Really, it is a mishap of offering,
and those, which are not fit for offering —
he is not occupied with them,
this one, which is fit for offering —
he is occupied with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם תַּקָּלָה דְּהַקְרָבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 10 by choosing the first option and showing why it applies only here.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: animals fit for offering compared with animals not fit for offering
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fear of offering would apply to every grazing animal.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only animals still fit for offering keep a person's attention, so only they bring a real risk of being wrongly offered.
steps.whatToRemember: The decree of תקלה here means the fear that someone will wrongly offer an animal that still looks fit to be offered.

steps.title: Attempt to show that worrying about mishap is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that fear of תקלה is a dispute between תנאים. Two ברייתות disagree whether a leftover קרבן פסח that was not offered on פסח שני may be offered the next year.
steps.simpleTranslation: And worrying about a mishap is itself a dispute of תנאים. One ברייתא teaches: a פסח that was not offered on the first פסח is offered on the second. If not on the second, it is offered the next year. Another ברייתא teaches: it is not offered. Is it not that they argue about mishap?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two ברייתות that seem to contradict each other. It suggests they argue about whether we fear a mishap from keeping an animal for a whole year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Keeping a קרבן פסח for a year is like keeping the פר and שעיר: someone might offer it wrongly in the meantime. The ברייתא that allows offering it next year would not fear תקלה. The one that forbids it would fear תקלה. If this is right, רבא's decree follows only one side.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים
The second פסח (14 אייר) for those who missed the first
Another ברייתא teaches
Is it not that...? (proposing a reading)

phrases.english: And the issue of mishap itself is a dispute of תנאים.
For one ברייתא teaches:
A פסח that was not offered on the first —
should be offered on the second;
if not on the second, it should be offered the next year.
And another ברייתא teaches: it should not be offered.
Is it not that they disagree about mishap?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַקָּלָה עַצְמָהּ תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having explained what the mishap is, the גמרא now asks whether the fear of mishap is itself debated.
steps.raayaObject: That fear of תקלה is a dispute between תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: Two contradicting ברייתות about offering a leftover קרבן פסח the next year
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a challenge to רבא. It only claims that רבא's idea matches one side of an older dispute.

steps.title: No, the ברייתות follow רבי and רבנן in a different dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. It is possible that no one worries about תקלה. The two ברייתות follow רבי and רבנן, who argue about whether the lamb could still be young enough to be offered the next year.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees we do [not] worry about mishap. Here they argue in the dispute of רבי and רבנן, and it is not difficult: this one is רבי, that one is רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the proof from Step 12. It gives a different reason the two ברייתות disagree, one that has nothing to do with תקלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קרבן פסח must be under a year old. According to רבי, the lamb can still be under a year old by next פסח, so it may be offered then. Commentators connect this to how a leap year is counted. According to רבנן, it will surely be too old, so it cannot be offered. The disagreement is about the animal's age, not about fearing a mishap.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
We are concerned / we worry
A dispute
This one follows ... that one follows (resolving a contradiction)

phrases.english: No, everyone agrees we are [not] concerned about mishap,
phrases.notes: The bracketed word is a text correction. Without it, the claim would be that everyone does worry about mishap.

phrases.english: and here, in the dispute of רבי and the Rabbis,
they disagree,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא רַבִּי, הָא רַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: and it is not difficult: this one is רבי, that one is the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא חָיְישִׁינַן לְתַקָּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in Step 12 that fear of תקלה is a dispute between תנאים.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the claim that the ברייתות argue about תקלה. It does not touch רבא's decree itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The contradiction can be explained by a different dispute, about the lamb's age next year (רבי compared with רבנן).

steps.title: The leftover money proves the rejection wrong
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rejection in Step 13 using a ברייתא that applies the same dispute to leftover money.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא: 'And the same is true of the money'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rejection from Step 13. That rejection said the two ברייתות argue about the lamb's age, not about תקלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא says the same dispute also applies to money set aside to buy a קרבן פסח. Money never gets older, so the argument between רבי and רבנן about the lamb's age cannot apply to it. So the age explanation cannot be the real reason for the dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught (in a ברייתא)? This introduces a challenge from a source.
Money. Here it means coins set aside to buy a קרבן פסח.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think money has an 'age' problem. That is exactly the point: money cannot become too old, so the age explanation fails.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא:
And the same is true of the money!
phrases.notes: Leftover money for a פסח is subject to the same dispute about keeping it for next year.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: וְכֵן הַמָּעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rejection in Step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתות argue only about the lamb's age (רבי vs. רבנן)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same dispute applies to money, which has no age. So age cannot be the reason for the dispute.

steps.title: Conclusion: the תנאים argue about the fear of a mishap
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the dispute really is about whether we fear תקלה, and accepts this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, must we not learn from this that they argue about the fear of a mishap? Yes, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: With the age explanation gone, the גמרא returns to its first proof from Step 12 and confirms it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only reason left that fits both the lamb and the money is the fear that someone might misuse it later (תקלה). So the תנאים really do argue about whether we make a rule out of fear of תקלה. The repeated 'שמע מינה' means the גמרא accepts this.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it so that... This brings the only answer left.
A mishap. Here it means fear that someone might use the item wrongly later.
Learn from this. When repeated at the end, the גמרא is agreeing.

steps.whatToRemember: Whether we fear תקלה is a real dispute between תנאים. This is proven from leftover פסח money, where the animal's age plays no role.

phrases.english: Rather, must we not learn from this —
that they argue about the fear of a mishap?
Yes, learn from this.
phrases.notes: The גמרא accepts the conclusion.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ בְּתַקָּלָה פְּלִיגִי שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final conclusion from the challenge in Step 14
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The two ברייתות argue about whether we worry about תקלה, as Step 12 first suggested.

steps.title: The כהן גדול confesses over the scapegoat
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה describes the כהן גדול leaning on the שעיר המשתלח and saying the confession for all of Israel.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: He comes to the scapegoat, leans both hands on it, and confesses. He would say: 'Please, ה׳! Your people, the house of Israel, have sinned, done wrong, and rebelled before You. Please, ה׳! Forgive the sins, wrongs, and rebellions that Your people, the house of Israel, sinned, did wrong, and rebelled before You. As it is written in the תורה of משה Your servant: For on this day He will atone for you, to purify you from all your sins; before ה׳ you will be pure.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It continues the יום כיפור service: the כהן גדול now confesses over the שעיר המשתלח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the third וידוי of the day. The first two were for the כהן גדול himself and for the כהנים. This one is for all of Israel. The structure is the same: three kinds of sin (חטא, עון, פשע), a request for forgiveness, and a פסוק that ends with 'לפני ה׳ תטהרו'.

keyTerms.meaning: The scapegoat that is sent off to the wilderness on יום כיפור.
Leaning one's hands on the animal (here: וְסוֹמֵךְ).
Confession of sins (here: וּמִתְוַדֶּה).
Three levels of sin: by mistake, on purpose, and in rebellion.

steps.whyThisMatters: The words of this וידוי are the source for the סדר העבודה we say in מוסף on יום כיפור.

phrases.english: משנה:
He comes over to the scapegoat,
leans both his hands on it, and confesses.
And this is what he would say:
Please, ה׳!
phrases.notes: Here the כהן גדול said the real Name of ה׳, the שם המפורש.

phrases.english: They have sinned, done wrong, and rebelled before You,
Your people, the house of Israel.
Please, ה׳!
Please forgive the sins, the wrongs, and the rebellions
that they sinned, did wrong, and rebelled before You,
Your people, the house of Israel,
as it is written in the Torah of Moses Your servant:
"For on this day He will atone for you
to purify you from all your sins;
before ה׳ you will be pure." (ויקרא טז:ל)

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בָּא לוֹ אֵצֶל שָׂעִיר הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול leans both hands on the שעיר המשתלח and confesses for all of Israel using the set text.

steps.title: The people bow when they hear the Name of ה׳
steps.stepSummary: When the people in the עזרה heard the שם המפורש, they bowed down and said בשכמל״ו.
steps.simpleTranslation: The כהנים and the people standing in the עזרה, when they heard the special Name of ה׳ coming from the mouth of the כהן גדול, would kneel, bow down, and fall on their faces. They would say: 'Blessed is the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues. It describes how the crowd reacted each time the כהן גדול said the שם המפורש during the confession.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שם המפורש was only said aloud in the מקדש, so hearing it was an awesome moment. The crowd answered with full bowing and the praise 'ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד', which was said in the מקדש instead of 'אמן'.

keyTerms.meaning: The courtyard of the בית המקדש.
The explicit, real Name of ה׳, said aloud as it is written.
Kneeling and bowing down.

keyTerms.term: בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד
keyTerms.meaning: 'Blessed is the name of His glorious kingdom forever.' The response said in the מקדש.

phrases.english: And the כהנים and the people standing in the courtyard,
when they would hear the explicit Name
coming out of the mouth of the כהן גדול,
would kneel and bow down
and fall on their faces, and say:
"Blessed is the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַכֹּהֲנִים וְהָעָם הָעוֹמְדִים בָּעֲזָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה by describing the crowd's response to the confession
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When people hear the שם המפורש, they bow fully and say בשכמל״ו.

steps.title: Who may lead the scapegoat away
steps.stepSummary: The goat is handed to the person who will lead it. By law anyone may do this, but the כהנים גדולים made it a fixed custom that only כהנים would.
steps.simpleTranslation: He handed it to the person who would lead it away. Everyone is fit to lead it. But the כהנים גדולים made it a fixed practice and did not let a regular Israelite lead it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to the next stage: handing the goat over to be taken to the wilderness. It also says who is allowed to do this job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה separates the law from the custom. By law anyone, even a non-כהן, may lead the goat. The כהנים גדולים, however, set up a custom that kept the job for כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: He handed it over.
The one who leads it (to the wilderness).
A fixed practice or set custom.
Here: a regular Jew who is not a כהן.

steps.confusionAlert: 'יִשְׂרָאֵל' here does not mean the whole Jewish people. It means a Jew who is not a כהן.

phrases.english: He handed it to the one who would lead it.
Everyone is fit to lead it,
but the כהנים גדולים made it a fixed practice,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הָיוּ מַנִּיחִין אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְהוֹלִיכוֹ.
phrases.english: and they would not let a regular Israelite lead it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְסָרוֹ לְמִי שֶׁהָיָה מוֹלִיכוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה to the next stage of the service
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By law anyone may lead the שעיר המשתלח. In practice, the כהנים גדולים kept the job for כהנים.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: an Israelite once led the goat
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי tells of a time when a man named ערסלא, a non-כהן, led the goat away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: There was a case where ערסלא led it, and he was a regular Israelite.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי adds a story. It shows that the custom of using only כהנים was not always kept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story backs up the legal point that a non-כהן is fit to lead the goat. It also shows that the custom of the כהנים גדולים was not always followed.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident or story, often brought as proof of the law.
The name of the Israelite who once led the goat.

phrases.english: רבי יוסי said:
There was a case where ערסלא led it,
and he was a regular Israelite.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מַעֲשֶׂה וְהוֹלִיכוֹ עַרְסְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a story that limits the custom described in Step 18
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A non-כהן did lead the goat in practice, which shows such a person is fit to do so.

steps.title: A ramp was built because of the Babylonian Jews
steps.stepSummary: A raised ramp was built for the goat because Babylonian Jews would pull its hair and shout at it to take their sins and go.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they built a ramp for it because of the Babylonians. They would pull at its hair and say to it: 'Take and go out! Take and go out!'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains why a special raised ramp was built to lead the goat out of ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Babylonian Jews in ירושלים were eager for the goat to carry their sins away quickly, so they grabbed at its hair and urged it on. This crowding was disrespectful and slowed the goat down. The ramp let it pass above the crowd.

keyTerms.meaning: A ramp or raised walkway.
Babylonian Jews (living in ירושלים).
'Take (our sins) and go out!'

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה moves step by step: the וידוי over the שעיר המשתלח, the crowd bowing at the שם המפורש, handing the goat to its leader (anyone may lead it by law, though the כהנים kept the job), and a ramp to protect it from the eager crowd.

phrases.english: And they made a ramp for it
because of the Babylonians,
who would pull at its hair
and say to it:
Take and go out, take and go out!
phrases.notes: Meaning: take our sins and go.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֶבֶשׁ עָשׂוּ לוֹ מִפְּנֵי הַבָּבְלִיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with a practical detail about leading the goat out
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ramp was built for the שעיר המשתלח so the Babylonian Jews could not pull at it.

steps.title: Why are the כהנים not mentioned in the confession?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the confession over the שעיר המשתלח does not mention 'בני אהרן', and asks which תנא the משנה follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Notice that the כהן גדול does not say 'the children of אהרן, Your holy people.' Which תנא taught this משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out something missing from the confession in the משנה and asks whose opinion the משנה follows. This sets up the next step, where an answer is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the confession over his own bull, the כהן גדול did mention 'בני אהרן'. Here, over the שעיר המשתלח, he says only 'עמך בית ישראל'. The גמרא wants to know which view of the כהנים' atonement explains this difference.

keyTerms.meaning: The תלמוד's discussion of the משנה
Whereas; but notice that
The children of אהרן, meaning the כהנים
Who is the תנא? (Whose opinion is this?)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two confessions. Over his own bull the כהן גדול did mention the כהנים. The question here is only about the confession over the שעיר המשתלח.

phrases.english: Gemara:
phrases.notes: Opening of the גמרא on the משנה

phrases.english: Whereas 'the children of Aaron, Your holy people'
phrases.notes: The phrase used in the earlier confession over the bull

phrases.english: he does not say.
Who is the Tanna?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִילּוּ ״בְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן עַם קְדוֹשֶׁךָ״ לָא קָאָמַר. מַאן תַּנָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the confession text from the משנה in Step 16 and examines its wording
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view explains why the כהנים are not mentioned in the confession over the שעיר המשתלח

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: The משנה does not follow רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה says the משנה cannot follow רבי יהודה, because רבי יהודה holds that the כהנים also get atonement through the שעיר המשתלח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: It is not like רבי יהודה. If it were like רבי יהודה, he says the כהנים do get atonement through the שעיר המשתלח.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers the question. He says the משנה follows the opinion that disagrees with רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that the כהנים are atoned for by the שעיר המשתלח, just like the rest of Israel. If so, the confession should mention them by name. Since the משנה leaves them out, רבי ירמיה concludes it follows the view that the כהנים are not atoned for through this goat.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who answers the question
Not in accordance with
For if
Atonement

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
It is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda,
for if it were like Rabbi Yehuda, didn't he say:
They (the priests) have atonement
through the scapegoat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'מאן תנא' question of Step 21
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה is not like רבי יהודה, since he holds the כהנים are atoned for through the שעיר המשתלח and so would need to be mentioned

steps.title: אביי: The כהנים are already included in 'Your people Israel'
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that the משנה can follow רבי יהודה, since the כהנים are part of 'עמך ישראל' and do not need to be named separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: You can even say it follows רבי יהודה. Are the כהנים not part of 'Your people Israel'?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רבי ירמיה. He says the missing words prove nothing, so the משנה can still follow רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ירמיה assumed that if the כהנים were atoned for, they would have to be named. אביי says the general phrase 'עמך בית ישראל' already includes them. So leaving out 'בני אהרן' tells us nothing about whose opinion the משנה follows.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who disputes רבי ירמיה
Even if you say
Is that to say...? (a rhetorical question)
Included in

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ירמיה says the confession leaves out the כהנים because the משנה does not follow רבי יהודה. אביי says the כהנים are already included in 'עמך ישראל', so the משנה could follow anyone.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Even if you say it is Rabbi Yehuda,
is that to say the priests are not
included in 'Your people Israel'?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי ירמיה's conclusion in Step 22
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the משנה cannot follow רבי יהודה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It wrongly assumes the כהנים must be named separately, when 'עמך ישראל' already includes them
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Leaving out 'בני אהרן' does not prove the משנה goes against רבי יהודה

steps.title: A ברייתא: The word 'איש' allows a non-כהן to lead the goat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about handing over the goat, then brings a ברייתא that learns from 'איש' that a זר may lead it, and begins explaining 'עתי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'He handed it to the one who would lead it.' The רבנן taught: 'A man' comes to allow a non-כהן. 'Appointed'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה, about who leads the goat away. It brings a ברייתא that gives the source in the פסוק, word by word. This passage ends in the middle of the explanation of 'עתי'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in Step 18 said that by law anyone may lead the goat. This ברייתא shows where that comes from: the פסוק says 'איש', a general word, which includes a זר. The next word, 'עתי', is about to be explained.

keyTerms.meaning: He handed it over
The רבנן taught (introduces a ברייתא)
To make fit; to allow
A non-כהן
Appointed, prepared (from the פסוק in ויקרא טז:כא)

phrases.english: He handed it to the one who would lead it.
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה (see Step 18)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
'A man' comes to allow a non-priest;
'appointed' comes to teach...
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud

steps.triggerLanguage: מְסָרוֹ לְמִי שֶׁמּוֹלִיכוֹ. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the confession discussion and turns to the next line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the word 'איש' in the פסוק, a non-כהן is allowed to lead the שעיר המשתלח
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives the source for the משנה's rule that by law anyone may lead the goat, even though the כהנים made it their custom to do it themselves.
